header.stance: 全面降溫讓Fed多些時間，燃料風險卻再起

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## CPI全面降溫，7月升息風險退後，油價卻再上漲

6月通膨放緩不只來自汽油，也延伸至住宅與服務，美債週二上漲，Fed得以爭取更多等待時間。2年期殖利率下降8個基點至4.18%，10年期下降4個基點至4.58%。核心CPI月增率為零，使Waller前一天警告帶來的升息急迫性明顯降低。

漲勢未能維持早盤全部幅度。Kevin Warsh在國會肯定通膨資料，但仍將升息保留為工具，海灣地區再度交火又推高油價。2年期殖利率一度降至4.14%，終場回升；30年期僅下降2個基點至5.08%。6月降溫為政策買到時間，卻尚未反映最新燃料衝擊。

信用買方也區分發行人。Goldman Sachs以龐大訂單完成$100億發債，Prime Data Centers卻先縮減規模、再延後交易。日本20年期標售強勁，為日債漲勢提供退休基金政策言論以外的實際支撐。Fed眼前風險降低有利價格，並不代表每家企業、每個天期都同樣容易融資。

## 汽油之外，住宅與服務也放慢漲價

6月整體CPI月減0.4%，反轉5月增加0.5%，年增率由4.2%降至3.5%；核心物價月變化為零，年增率由2.9%降至2.6%。實質平均時薪年增0.1%。市場重估接下來幾次Fed會議，主要依據是物價降溫的廣度，而非只有能源。

能源月減5.7%，其中汽油下降9.7%。住宅成本僅增0.1%，為2021年1月以來最小月增幅：屋主等值租金增加0.2%、租金增加0.1%，旅館住宿下降2.3%。汽車保險下跌2.0%，通訊下跌1.5%，服飾下跌0.6%，中古車下跌0.2%。排除住宅與能源的服務價格下降0.2%，追平疫情開始以來最大跌幅。

部分年增率仍高，能源15.7%、食品3.0%、住宅3.3%、機票26.5%。電腦軟體與配件6月上漲2.3%，年增17.4%。這些項目讓科技需求、供給限制與再起的運輸成本，仍有可能在廣泛月度改善後，維持局部物價壓力。

資料公布前後，7月升息機率由約40%降至20%以下，期貨將較可能的時間移向9月或10月。2年期殖利率觸及4.14%後回升。槓桿基金進場前持有去年9月以來最大的空頭部位，因此基本面意外，也可能獲得部位調整的助力。

Warsh在三小時聽證中表示，通膨優於預期，但利率仍是處理持續物價壓力的工具。他沒有暗示即將升息，部分經濟學家也認為新指引有限。不過，他不願宣告抗通膨完成，加上油價上漲，限制了早盤漲勢，同時仍讓7月升息明顯較不可能。

### 前端領漲，長天期實質利率仍高

2年期終場下降8個基點至4.18%，5年期下降6個基點至4.31%，10年期下降4個基點至4.58%，30年期下降2個基點至5.08%。2年與10年期利差擴大4個基點至40，2年與30年期擴大6個基點至90。較一週前，2年期低1個基點，5、10及30年期仍高4、3及3個基點；一個月變化也仍全面為正，從2年期上升9個基點，到30年期上升11個基點。

10年期實質殖利率下降3個基點至2.33%，損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點至2.25%；5年與7年期實質殖利率也下降3個基點，至2.03%及2.17%，20年與30年期下降2個基點，至2.67%及2.87%。10年期實質殖利率仍較一週前高3個基點、一個月前高16個基點，30年期則高3及14個基點。即期政策壓力減輕，貢獻指標券大部分漲幅，卻未消除長天期要求的實質報酬。

國庫券也反映升息時間延後。4週與8週期維持3.70%及3.72%，6週期上升2個基點至3.72%；13週與17週期各下降5個基點，6個月下降8個基點，一年期下降10個基點至4.02%。

$950億42天期標售的最高利率為3.640%，投標倍數2.84，該利率配售比例63.10%。競標得標合計$915.60億，包括間接投標人$662.53億、交易商$237.44億，以及直接投標人$15.63億。該券7月16日交割、8月27日到期。

小企業對眼前定價的看法較不溫和。NFIB樂觀指數上升2.1點至97.4，接近長期平均，營商環境與實質銷售預期改善。但淨38%的業者已提高價格，為2023年1月以來最高；計畫調漲的比例則下降2個百分點至32%。較佳銷售期待，與當前定價偏強、未來意向轉弱同時存在。

Michael Barr認為，AI尚未在全經濟造成大規模工作取代，但部分年輕人的入行變得更困難。受控環境下的龐大生產力改善，也不代表採用已普遍：研究所學歷者的使用率，遠高於最高學歷僅為高中的勞工。技術擴散不均，使潛在供給能增加多少、誰能受惠於投資熱潮，都更難判斷。

## Goldman訂單充足，Prime Data Centers卻延後發債

Goldman Sachs在股票交易創紀錄、固定收益、外匯與商品收入年增32%之後，分三部分發行$100億債券，天期由6至31年。訂單高峰約$320億，最長券以美債加113個基點定價，比初始指引收窄22個基點。

這使Goldman今年美元投資級發債達$440億，也占週二三筆美國投資級交易合計$139億的大部分。即使本月先前企業供給已多，熟悉且獲利強勁的銀行發行人，仍可大量發行長天期債並收緊價格。

Prime Data Centers的結果不同。公司先尋求依挪威法發行$6億債券，再縮至$5億，最後因投資人不接受條件而延後。唯一承銷商Arctic Securities表示市場環境轉差，可能很快重返，也可能等到暑假後。

相較之下，H.I.G.控制的PolarDC在5月擴大北歐高收益債至€8億，當時創市場紀錄。Prime自己的Elk Grove子公司，也在6月為芝加哥專案擴大發債至$9億，並有15年CoreWeave租約支持。但主要客戶Meta發展自有雲端業務之際，CoreWeave歐元債已跌至面額約95.7%。今年資料中心開發商在美國高收益市場已籌約$300億，租戶知名、產業成長強，已不保證投資組合還有額度承接。

LQD上漲0.23%、HYG上漲0.20%、JNK上漲0.15%，廣泛信用受惠於美債與股市上漲；初級市場的執行結果，則凸顯銀行獲利實力與AI集中曝險的差別。

### 外資偏好長期證券，短期美元部位卻縮減

美東16:00公布的5月TIC顯示淨流入$1,322億，民間流入$1,720億，超過官方流出$399億。外資買進$2,628億長期美國證券，其中美國中長期公債淨買進$566億。晚盤資料補充了較高殖利率吸引海外需求的證據，並非早盤CPI漲勢的起因。

同時，外資持有國庫券減少$435億，美國銀行對外國居民的淨美元負債下降$700億。長期證券需求增加，與較短美元部位收縮可以同時發生；當天6週期標售需求足夠，也不支持把這些資金流解讀為全面撤離美元資產。

美國小企業借款仍弱。NFIB受訪者僅22%固定借款，比歷史平均低12個百分點；平均短期貸款利率下降0.4個百分點至7.4%，為2022年10月以來最低。銷售預期較佳、利率降低，尚未促成固定借款的普遍增加。

地方政府債估值則呈現需求強勁的另一面。7月10日，最高評等10年期免稅債殖利率僅為美債的65.5%，低於五年平均71%；30年期相對公司債也接近三年來最昂貴。基金與ETF流入吸收了接近紀錄的供給，但機構買方愈來愈挑價格，部分策略師偏好先持短期美債，等比率正常化。

## 日債投標強勁，為新增買方討論提供實際依據

日本20年期標售投標倍數由2.97升至4.52，價格尾差由0.24縮至零。約¥7,000億交易提供了實際需求訊號，20年與30年期殖利率盤中最多下降18個基點，至3.565%及3.725%，40年期下降10個基點。

片山皋月提出把日債納入個人稅惠帳戶的構想，也表示GPIF必要時可調整投資組合。Societe Generale估計，不必改變策略基準，國內公債仍有最高¥12.3兆加碼空間，假設持有比重由26.9%提高至既有區間上限31%。這是現行規則下的容量，不是已宣布的購買計畫；實際支撐與海外債券需求的影響，取決於規模及速度。

強勁標售減輕了財政支出、弱勢日圓與日本央行漸進正常化帶來的即時壓力。長期配置問題尚未解決，但相較只有政策言論，投標結果更能證明買方回來。

### 英國財政風險，已反映在實際投資組合調整

Andy Burnham即將進入唐寧街之際，據報內部預測將第四季通膨升至3.2%，預期英債殖利率提高、年底前至少升息一次。借款成本已使政府£236億的財政規則緩衝至少減少£55億；海灣供應中斷威脅能源成本時，新財相可能放寬政策又增加不確定性。

Rathbones旗下£36億Multi-Asset Strategic Growth基金，英債比重由12月9.2%降至5月6%，也在£98億多元資產組合中出售長英債。存續期間降至5至6年，低於英債指標逾7年，主權配置移向紐西蘭、澳洲、挪威，最近也加入美國。部位保留較短天期收益，同時減少對英國預算鬆綁的曝險。

Andrew Bailey在美東16:00演說指出，金融危機後潛在供給成長由原本2.8%降至1.3%，生產力貢獻由2.4個百分點降至0.4個百分點。他強調具韌性且合比例的銀行監管，有助維持放款並改善成長能力。

美國收盤後，Rachel Reeves提出英國首筆數位主權債於2027年初前發行的計畫，並設想後續發行與代幣化存款試辦。擬議資本調整估計最多可支持£1,500億銀行放款，擴大的Growth Guarantee Scheme則以每年£35億小企業信貸為目標。這些資本市場與貸款措施，與眼前英債融資問題並行，尚非直接解方。

### 中國供給可能創紀錄，央行先補流動性

中國人民銀行宣布人民幣1.4兆元6個月買斷式逆回購，扣除到期後淨投放5,000億元，加上先前3個月操作，7月透過這項工具的淨投放將達7,000億元。稅款、信貸擴張與政府債務需求，都提高了現金需要。

美國收盤後公布的估計，將第三季中央及地方政府淨發債列為人民幣4.2兆至4.4兆元，高於去年同期紀錄。上半年已完成全年目標約52%，地方政府通常希望10月前完成；10年期殖利率也由十個月低點回升至約1.74%。官方流動性可協助吸收，卻不會讓供給消失。

歐洲政策定價仍對能源敏感。布蘭特接近$90之際，交易員已把英國央行與ECB緊縮預期提前；一位波蘭決策者也認為，即使通膨在目標，升息仍比降息更可能。美國CPI偏弱可以延後Fed，卻無法消除各地國內與進口物價壓力。

## 美債殖利率下降支撐新興市場，印尼與塞內加爾仍受本地限制

CPI公布後，EMB上漲0.20%，美元指數下降0.34%至100.94。巴西里耳盤中最多升值1.4%，南非幣與墨西哥披索也上漲。較低美債殖利率與較弱美元改善共同融資環境，但後來油價回升、海灣再遭攻擊，限制了漲幅。

印尼雖受惠標普維持評等，10年期本地殖利率仍上升3個基點至7.26%，買方關注油價的通膨效果。政府強調審慎、彈性發債，但較低美債前端利率，無法消除進口燃料壓力，或已拖累匯率的國內疑慮。

塞內加爾國際債權人開始非正式討論組成小組，政府也考慮聘請顧問。2024年發現的$70億未揭露債務，使公共債務升至GDP 132%，IMF暫停$18億計畫。主權利差超過1,500個基點，區域市場對較長債務的需求轉弱；在已相當嚴峻的融資問題中，債權人開始協調才是新的進展。

政府尋求新的IMF融資，但國內對債務處理仍有分歧，使談判更複雜。區域借款將更多主權風險移至本地資產負債表，全球新興市場單日改善，難以替代可信揭露、官方資金與取得共識的到期安排。

宏都拉斯則希望運用較平穩的窗口，提出買回最高$7億2027年票據，以成功發行新全球債為條件，將是2024年以來首度外部發債。再融資可延後到期高峰，但須看新債能否完成與整體成本。2026年新興主權及企業供給已創紀錄達$4,914億，交易仍置身擁擠的發債日程。

## 股市歡迎CPI降溫，原油再帶來下一輪物價風險

S&P 500上漲0.38%，Nasdaq 100上漲1.10%，半導體上漲2.54%，VIX下降3.85%至16.50。Fed即期風險降低支持科技股，銀行獲利也讓債券反彈與成長信心並存。

WTI仍上漲1.54%至$79.34，布蘭特上漲1.72%至$84.73；盤中報導油價超過$87，汽油、柴油與航空燃油反彈更大。Donald Trump不再推動荷莫茲貨物20%收費，移除一項成本威脅，但油輪攻擊與持續空襲仍保留供應風險。6月CPI反映先前汽油跌價，並非最新戰事。

美元降至100.94，實質殖利率下降，黃金上漲1.60%至$4,061.10。金價與股票同漲、波動率降低，結合了利率緩解與殘留的地緣避險。早盤美債漲勢部分回吐，也顯示投資人仍在衡量新燃料壓力與6月較廣泛的通膨放緩。

## 生產者價格與Fed官員，檢驗降溫能否延續

7月15日美東08:30公布PPI與紐約州製造業調查，10:00為Warsh參議院聽證，13:00為Lisa Cook經濟展望演說，14:00公布褐皮書。PPI中影響核心PCE的項目、工廠定價與地區報告，將有助判斷6月消費物價偏弱是否繼續擴散。市場已大幅降低7月升息機率，Fed如何解讀更值得注意。

EIA石油庫存於7月15日美東10:30公布；7月17日08:30進出口物價、10:00密西根通膨預期初值。成品油庫存、煉廠運作與家庭預期，將協助衡量6月CPI尚未涵蓋的物價衝擊。

財政部7月15日美東11:30發行$720億17週期國庫券；週二$950億6週期於7月16日交割，當天11:30再標售合計$2,100億4週及8週期。相鄰天期供給陸續到來，投標與擔保融資將顯示現金需求是否仍從容。
zh-TW.methodology_note: 除非另有註明，市場水準均以紐約收盤為準。

overall_summary.headline: CPI降溫不限汽油，7月升息風險降低，油價卻續漲
overall_summary.session_narrative:
6月CPI降溫涵蓋住宅、商品與服務，不只汽油。整體物價月減0.4%，核心持平，7月升息機率降至20%以下。2年期殖利率下降8個基點至4.18%，10年期下降4個基點至4.58%，主要來自實質利率。

Warsh肯定資料，但仍保留升息工具，海灣再度交火也推高油價。Goldman Sachs以約$320億訂單完成$100億發債，Prime Data Centers卻先縮規模、再延期，顯示強勁銀行獲利與已大量配置AI的投資組合之間，融資條件不同。

日本20年期標售投標倍數4.52，為日債漲勢提供實證；GPIF可能買入仍有條件。英國財政風險促使投資人縮短英債部位，中國則在大量供給前準備流動性。PPI、Fed官員與燃料庫存，將檢驗CPI緩解能否延續超過一個月。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Broad CPI Relief Pushes July Hike Risk Back, Even as Oil Rises

Treasuries rallied Tuesday after June inflation slowed well beyond gasoline, giving the Fed room to wait before raising rates. Two-year yields fell 8 basis points to 4.18%, while the 10-year declined 4 to 4.58%. Flat monthly core CPI and softer shelter and services prices sharply reduced the urgency that Waller's warning had created a day earlier.

The rally faded from its early strength. Kevin Warsh welcomed the inflation report in congressional testimony but kept rate increases among the available tools, while renewed Gulf fighting lifted oil again. The two-year traded as low as 4.14% before closing higher; the 30-year recovered only 2 basis points to 5.08%. June's disinflation bought time without capturing the latest fuel shock.

Credit buyers also distinguished between borrowers. Goldman Sachs raised $10 billion with a large orderbook, while Prime Data Centers cut a proposed bond and then postponed it. Japan's strong 20-year auction gave its bond rally support beyond pension-policy talk. Across markets, lower immediate Fed risk helped prices, but it did not make every issuer or maturity equally easy to finance.

## Shelter and Services Join Gasoline in Slowing Inflation

Headline CPI fell 0.4% in June after May's 0.5% rise, slowing annual inflation to 3.5% from 4.2%. Core prices were unchanged on the month and rose 2.6% over the year, down from 2.9%. Real average hourly earnings increased 0.1% annually. The breadth of the price slowdown, rather than energy alone, drove the repricing of the next Fed meetings.

Energy fell 5.7%, including a 9.7% gasoline decline. Shelter increased just 0.1%, the smallest monthly gain since January 2021: owners' equivalent rent rose 0.2%, rent 0.1% and lodging fell 2.3%. Vehicle insurance declined 2.0%, communication 1.5%, apparel 0.6% and used vehicles 0.2%. Services excluding housing and energy dropped 0.2%, matching their largest decline since the pandemic began.

Several annual rates remained high. Energy was up 15.7%, food 3.0%, shelter 3.3% and airfares 26.5%. Computer software and accessories rose 2.3% in June and 17.4% over the year. Those categories left scope for technology demand, supply constraints and renewed transport costs to keep parts of inflation elevated after the broad monthly improvement.

July hike pricing fell below 20% from roughly 40% immediately around the release, with futures shifting the more likely timing to September or October. The two-year yield touched 4.14% before retracing. Leveraged funds had entered with their largest short stance since September, giving the fundamental surprise potential support from position adjustment.

During three hours of testimony, Warsh said the report was better than expected but kept rates among the tools available against persistent inflation. He did not signal an imminent increase; some economists saw little new guidance. His refusal to declare the job finished, alongside rising oil, helped limit the early rally while leaving July tightening much less likely.

### Front-End Gains Leave Long Real Yields Elevated

The two-year closed down 8 basis points at 4.18%, five years fell 6 to 4.31%, 10 years declined 4 to 4.58% and 30 years eased 2 to 5.08%. The move widened 2s10s by 4 basis points to 40 and 2s30s by 6 to 90. Over the week, two years were down 1 basis point, but five, 10 and 30 years remained up 4, 3 and 3. Monthly increases persisted across the curve, from 9 basis points at two years to 11 at 30 years.

Ten-year real yield fell 3 basis points to 2.33% and breakeven inflation declined 1 to 2.25%. Five- and seven-year real yields also fell 3, to 2.03% and 2.17%; 20 and 30 years eased 2, to 2.67% and 2.87%. Ten-year real yield was still 3 basis points higher over the week and 16 over the month, while the 30-year remained up 3 and 14. Less immediate policy restraint accounted for most of the benchmark rally, without removing the return required at long maturities.

Bill yields reflected the same timing shift. Four and eight weeks held at 3.70% and 3.72%, and six weeks rose 2 basis points to 3.72%. Thirteen and 17 weeks each fell 5 basis points, six months declined 8 and one year dropped 10 to 4.02%.

The $95 billion 42-day auction cleared at a 3.640% high rate with 2.84 bid-to-cover and 63.10% allotted at that rate. Competitive awards totaled $91.560 billion, including $66.253 billion for indirect bidders, $23.744 billion for dealers and $1.563 billion for direct bidders. The bill settles July 16 and matures August 27.

Small businesses offered a less benign view of current pricing. NFIB optimism rose 2.1 points to 97.4, near its long-run average, as expectations for conditions and real sales improved. A net 38% of owners had raised prices, the highest since January 2023, although the share planning increases fell 2 points to 32%. Better sales expectations coexisted with firm current pricing and softer intentions.

Michael Barr saw little economy-wide job displacement from AI but more difficult entry for some young workers. Large productivity gains in controlled settings had not implied universal adoption: usage was far more common among workers with graduate degrees than those educated only through high school. The uneven diffusion complicated the outlook for potential supply and who would benefit from the investment boom.

## Goldman Finds Deep Demand While Prime Data Centers Delays Its Bond

Goldman Sachs sold $10 billion across three tranches spanning six to 31 years after record equity-trading results and 32% annual growth in fixed-income, currency and commodity revenue. Orders peaked near $32 billion. The longest tranche priced 113 basis points over Treasuries, 22 basis points inside initial talk.

The deal brought Goldman's year-to-date dollar investment-grade issuance to $44 billion and made up most of Tuesday's $13.9 billion across three US high-grade offerings. A familiar bank issuer with strong earnings could place substantial long duration and tighten pricing, even after heavy corporate supply earlier in the month.

Prime Data Centers faced a different response. It initially sought $600 million under Norwegian law, cut the proposed size to $500 million and then postponed the bond after investors rejected the terms. Sole manager Arctic Securities cited deteriorating conditions, leaving open a quick return or a wait until after summer.

That contrasted with H.I.G.-controlled PolarDC's upsized €800 million Nordic high-yield deal in May, then a market record. Prime's own Elk Grove subsidiary had raised an upsized $900 million in June against a Chicago project with a 15-year CoreWeave lease. CoreWeave's euro bonds had since fallen to about 95.7 as key customer Meta developed its own cloud business. With data-center developers already raising roughly $30 billion in US high yield that year, familiar tenants and strong sector growth no longer guaranteed room in investors' portfolios.

LQD gained 0.23%, HYG 0.20% and JNK 0.15%. Broad credit shared the Treasury and equity rally, while primary-market execution exposed the difference between bank earnings strength and concentrated AI exposure.

### Foreign Buyers Favor Long Securities as Short Dollar Balances Contract

May TIC data, released at 16:00 ET, showed a $132.2 billion net inflow. Private inflows of $172.0 billion outweighed $39.9 billion of official outflows. Foreign investors bought $262.8 billion of long-term US securities, including a net $56.6 billion of Treasury notes and bonds. The late release added evidence of overseas demand at elevated yields rather than explaining the morning CPI rally.

At the same time, foreign Treasury-bill holdings fell $43.5 billion and US banks' net dollar liabilities to foreign residents declined $70.0 billion. Demand for long securities and contraction in shorter dollar positions were occurring together. The day's adequate six-week auction also argued against treating those flows as a wholesale retreat from dollar assets.

US small-business borrowing remained subdued. Only 22% of NFIB respondents borrowed regularly, 12 percentage points below the historical average. The average short-maturity loan rate fell 0.4 percentage point to 7.4%, its lowest since October 2022. Better sales expectations and lower rates had yet to produce a broad increase in regular borrowing.

Municipal valuations showed the other side of strong demand. Top-rated 10-year tax-exempt bonds yielded 65.5% as much as Treasuries on July 10, versus a five-year average of 71%; 30-year munis were near their richest relative to corporate bonds in three years. Fund and ETF inflows had absorbed near-record supply, but institutional buyers were becoming more selective. Some strategists preferred short Treasuries until ratios normalized.

## Strong JGB Bidding Adds Substance to Japan's Buyer-Base Debate

Japan's 20-year auction drew 4.52 bid-to-cover, up from 2.97, and the price tail narrowed to zero from 0.24. The roughly ¥700 billion sale gave the bond rally a concrete demand signal. Twenty- and 30-year yields fell as much as 18 basis points to 3.565% and 3.725%, while 40 years declined 10 basis points.

Satsuki Katayama floated adding JGBs to tax-advantaged individual accounts and said GPIF could adjust its portfolio if needed. Societe Generale estimated up to ¥12.3 trillion of additional domestic government-bond buying without changing the strategic benchmark, assuming holdings rose from 26.9% to the 31% upper limit of the existing band. That was capacity under current rules, not an announced purchase program. Size and speed would determine the actual support and the implications for foreign-bond demand.

The strong auction relieved immediate pressure from fiscal spending, a weak yen and concerns about gradual BOJ normalization. It did not settle the longer-run allocation question, but it was firmer evidence of buyers returning than policy remarks alone.

### UK Fiscal Risk Produces an Actual Portfolio Shift

Ahead of Andy Burnham's move into Downing Street, reported internal forecasts put fourth-quarter inflation at 3.2%, anticipated higher gilt yields and at least one BOE increase by year-end. Higher borrowing costs had reduced the government's £23.6 billion fiscal-rule buffer by at least £5.5 billion. Possible loosening under a new chancellor added uncertainty while Gulf disruption threatened energy costs.

Rathbones reduced gilt exposure in its £3.6 billion Multi-Asset Strategic Growth fund to 6% in May from 9.2% in December, and sold long gilts across £9.8 billion of multi-asset portfolios. Duration was cut to five to six years versus more than seven for the gilt benchmark. Sovereign exposure shifted toward New Zealand, Australia, Norway and more recently the US. The positions retained shorter income while reducing exposure to a looser UK budget.

In a 16:00 ET speech, Andrew Bailey said potential-supply growth had slowed to 1.3% after the financial crisis from 2.8% before it, with productivity's contribution falling to 0.4 percentage point from 2.4. He emphasized resilient, proportionate bank regulation as a way to sustain lending and improve growth capacity.

After the US close, Rachel Reeves outlined plans for the first UK digital sovereign bond by early 2027, with further issuance envisaged and a tokenized-deposit pilot. Proposed capital changes were estimated to enable up to £150 billion of bank lending, while the expanded Growth Guarantee Scheme targeted £3.5 billion of annual small-business credit. These were capital-market and lending initiatives alongside, rather than a resolution of, the immediate gilt funding question.

### China Adds Liquidity Ahead of Record Supply

The PBOC announced a CNY1.4 trillion six-month outright reverse repo, providing CNY500 billion net of maturities. With an earlier three-month operation, July net additions through the tool would reach CNY700 billion. Tax payments, credit expansion and government-debt demand all increased the need for cash.

Estimates released after the US close put third-quarter central and local net issuance at CNY4.2 trillion–CNY4.4 trillion, above the prior year's record for the period. First-half sales had reached about 52% of the annual target, and local governments typically aim to finish by October. The 10-year yield had rebounded to around 1.74% from a 10-month low. Official liquidity could ease absorption without eliminating the supply.

European policy pricing remained sensitive to energy. Traders had brought BOE and ECB tightening forward as Brent approached $90, while a Polish policymaker considered an increase more likely than a cut despite inflation at target. A softer US CPI could delay the Fed without removing those domestic and imported-price pressures.

## Lower US Yields Help EM, but Indonesia and Senegal Face Local Constraints

EMB rose 0.20% and DXY fell 0.34% to 100.94 after CPI. Brazil's real gained as much as 1.4%, and the rand and Mexican peso also advanced. Lower Treasury yields and a weaker dollar improved the common financing backdrop, although rising oil and renewed Gulf attacks limited later gains.

Indonesia's 10-year domestic yield rose 3 basis points to 7.26% despite support from S&P's rating affirmation. Investors focused on oil's inflation effect. The government emphasized prudent, flexible issuance, but lower US front-end yields could not remove imported-fuel pressure or domestic concerns already weighing on the currency.

Senegal's international bondholders began informal discussions about forming a creditor group as the government considered hiring an adviser. The discovery of $7 billion of unreported debt in 2024 had pushed public debt to 132% of GDP and led to suspension of a $1.8 billion IMF program. Spreads exceeded 1,500 basis points, and demand for longer debt in the regional market was weakening. Creditor coordination was the new development in an already severe financing problem.

The authorities sought a new IMF facility, but disagreement at home over debt treatment complicated negotiations. Regional borrowing transferred more sovereign risk to local balance sheets. A better global EM session could offer little substitute for credible disclosure, official financing and an agreed maturity plan.

Honduras sought to use the calmer window differently, offering to repurchase up to $700 million of 2027 notes conditional on a new global issue, its first external sale since 2024. Refinancing could extend the maturity wall, but depended on placing new debt and its all-in cost. EM sovereign and corporate issuance had already reached a record $491.4 billion in 2026, making the transaction part of a crowded calendar.

## Equities Welcome CPI Relief While Oil Revives the Next Inflation Risk

The S&P 500 gained 0.38%, Nasdaq 100 rose 1.10% and semiconductors advanced 2.54%. VIX fell 3.85% to 16.50. Lower immediate Fed risk supported technology, while bank earnings helped keep the bond rally compatible with confidence in growth.

WTI nevertheless rose 1.54% to $79.34 and Brent gained 1.72% to $84.73. Intraday reporting put oil above $87 and described sharper rebounds in gasoline, diesel and jet fuel. Donald Trump backed away from the proposed 20% Hormuz cargo charge, removing one cost threat, but tanker attacks and continued strikes preserved the supply risk. June CPI reflected the earlier gasoline decline, not the latest fighting.

Gold gained 1.60% to $4,061.10 as the dollar fell to 100.94 and real yields declined. Its rise alongside equities and lower volatility combined rate relief with residual geopolitical hedging. The partial retracement of the early Treasury rally showed that investors were still weighing renewed fuel pressure against June's broader disinflation.

## Producer Prices and Fed Speakers Test the Breadth of Relief

PPI and the Empire State survey arrive July 15 at 08:30 ET, followed by Warsh's Senate testimony at 10:00, Lisa Cook's outlook speech at 13:00 and the Beige Book at 14:00. PPI categories that feed core PCE, factory pricing and regional reports will help determine whether June's consumer-price softness is broadening. Fed interpretation will matter after July tightening lost much of its market-implied probability.

The EIA petroleum report is due July 15 at 10:30 ET. Import and export prices follow July 17 at 08:30, then preliminary Michigan inflation expectations at 10:00. Product inventories, refinery operation and household expectations will help measure the inflation impulse not captured by June CPI.

Treasury sells $72 billion of 17-week bills July 15 at 11:30 ET. Tuesday's $95 billion six-week issue settles July 16, when combined four- and eight-week auctions offer another $210 billion at 11:30. Bidding and secured funding across the sequence will show whether cash demand remains comfortable as supply moves through adjacent maturities.
